thread:
Mei: heads-up — onboarding sampleapp spikes 429s on first-run with the JS SDK. steps: fresh creds, enable prefetch pagination + embeddings warm-up, then hammer with the sample flow. anyone seen this?
Owen: yep saw a pattern last week. looks like token-refresh + client-side concurrent paginator were both retrying aggressively. 429 flood from hosted side.
Alex: is this the same flow that uses cursor prefetching + parallel embed calls? that combo can blow past per-second quotas.
Mei: exact combo. JS sampleapp starts 8 parallel page fetches by default, then each page triggers an embed request to warm cache. result: ~24 concurrent calls.
Jordan: ouch. onboarding should default to conservative concurrency. we want a good first-time experience. can we mitigate in SDK or sampleapp?
Owen: two quick levers: 1) client-side limiter (leaky bucket/slot pool) and 2) small grace window for retry/backoff to let auth refresh finish.
Alex: agree. current JS SDK auth refresh triggers a hard-fail for in-flight requests (401 -> immediate retry loop). combine that with pagination prefetch and you get stampede.
Mei: repro logs: 
```
[2026-06-12T17:02:12Z] request page=1 status=401 token_refresh=start
[2026-06-12T17:02:12Z] retry id=abcd status=429 retry_after=0.5
[2026-06-12T17:02:13Z] token_refresh=done new_token_ttl=3600
[2026-06-12T17:02:13Z] request id=abcd status=200
```
Owen: that shows the window where retries pile up because clients don't defer retries while auth is in progress. propose add an SDK-level `graceWindowMs` that suppresses hot retries for auth-refresh events.
Alex: also add a sampleapp change: reduce default prefetch pages from 8 -> 2 and make concurrency max configurable by env var.
Jordan: sounds good. any concerns about changing default in sampleapp vs SDK? we should prefer SDK safety defaults so other apps benefit.
Mei: implemented a quick patch locally: 
```
clientOptions: {
  maxInFlight: 6,
  graceWindowMs: 1200,
  retry: { baseMs: 300, maxAttempts: 4 }
}
```
Mei: with that the repro stops spiking 429s during token refresh.
Owen: nice. can you open a tiny RFC/PR describing semantics? important to document how graceWindow interacts with standard retry-after header handling.
Mei: yep will do. draft PR #3725 with tests and note about pagination prefetch defaults.
Alex: small nit: ensure the grace window only collapses auth-related fast retries, not server-driven `retry-after` backoffs.
Mei: agreed. implementation checks for `authInProgress` flag. if server returns explicit `retry-after`, that still wins.
Jordan: can we include a short sample app tutorial change in onboarding docs? "If you see early 429s, try lowering PREFETCH_PAGES and enabling CLIENT_GRACE_WINDOW_MS" — that should help reduce support tickets.
Mei: adding that to the quickstart. also adding a one-liner in the SDK changelog.
ci-bot: deployment: canary sdk-js v1.12.4-grace-window patch deployed to staging — tests passed (:white_check_mark:)
Owen: can we also add telemetry event so we can measure how often graceWindow actually deflects retries? anonymous metric with counts would be helpful.
Mei: adding a counter `sdk.retry.grace_window_suppressed` + tag `auth_refresh` in the PR.
Alex: sweet. once PR lands, coordinate with docs and update sampleapp template. low-risk change but big DX win. :tada:
Jordan: thanks everyone. follow-up: Mei to add PR + docs, Owen to review, Alex to sign off on sampleapp defaults.
Mei: on it. will ping when PR is up. :rocket:
